claims.text: Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr exhibits 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
Untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr rapidly oxidizes at high temperatures.
Poor high-temperature oxidation resistance limits the practical use of cast HfNbTaTiZr.
A 100–200 nm Al2O3 coating can be deposited on cast HfNbTaTiZr by CVD at approximately 900–950 °C.
A graded interlayer or surface pretreatment will improve adhesion of the Al2O3 coating to HfNbTaTiZr.
The proposed deposition process will produce a uniformly adherent, dense Al2O3 film with a graded interface.
The dense Al2O3 film will act as a physical oxygen-diffusion barrier.
The graded interlayer will maintain coating adhesion and prevent thermal spallation.
Reducing oxygen ingress will markedly improve the oxidation resistance of HfNbTaTiZr at 1000 °C in air for exposures up to 500 hours.
The ultrathin coating will leave the alloy's underlying microstructure effectively unchanged.
Preserving the underlying microstructure will preserve room-temperature tensile ductility.
After coating and oxidation exposure, room-temperature tensile ductility will remain within 8–16%.
After coating and oxidation exposure, yield strength at 1000 °C and strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1 will remain within 163–530 MPa.
Thermal-expansion mismatch may eventually compromise the coating's barrier integrity.
